data.title: (Builder version) Esri Campus Tour
data.summary: An early morning walking tour of the Esri campus in Redlands, California

data.text: Sidewalk
Sunrise streaks the New York Street sidewalk at the north edge of Esri's campus in Redlands, California.
New York Street
The headquarters building, completed in 2010, unifies the campus. New York Street used to bisect the campus, but a portion of the street was closed, and the building straddles the old right of way.
Palms
Stately palm trees line New York Street and frame views of the headquarters building.
Wild iris
An iris blooms in an artificial pond by the entrance to headquarters, called Building Q.
View from the atrium
A four-story glass atrium affords views of New York Street and Redlands. A second-floor lounge faces north.
Auditorium
An intimate auditorium is used for company and Redlands community events.
Atrium view
Looking south through the glass atrium wall.
Staircase
A dramatic cantilevered staircase dominates the Building Q Atrium.
Geography
Near a back entrance to Esri's Cafe is this ivy-framed paean to the discipline that underlies Esri's products.
Landscaping for people
Esri's campus has numerous outdoor seating areas to encourage impromptu al fresco meetings.
Geranium and Building L
A bright flowering plant accents the entrance to Building L on the east side of the campus.
Inside the Cafe
The Cafe is a light-filled gathering place for coffee, lunch, and special events.
Glass and rock
Boulders provide a contrast to the clean lines of the Cafe. Landscape architect and Esri founder Jack Dangermond personally supervised their placement.
Flowering palm
An ornamental palm near the entrance to building M
Building M hallway
A typical Esri office area features wide hallways and small glassed-in offices, encouraging interaction among staff.
Courtyard pond
The peaceful courtyard between Buildings M and MA includes this artifical wetland.
Sunning turtles
The pond is home to several sun-seeking red-eared turtles.
Architecture as backdrop
Most of Esri's buildings are dark and unobtrusive, emphasizing the naturalistic landscape.
Working out
An ivy-colored gym at the campus's west end provides exercise equipment.
Living with nature
Building OA's dark walls set off a tree and a hummingbird feeder.
Artwork
A mobile stands near the entrance to Building O.
Building Q
The headquarters building is a dramatic exception to the subdued architecture of most of the campus. It was designed by the Danish firm HVIDT ARKITEKTER.
Headquarters entrance
A return to the main entrance of Building Q brings our campus tour to a close. We hope you can visit in person soon!
